body:
Just for a record, here's another example that will not work with this change:
1. Project is located in `~/projects/foo`
2. `.eslintrc` file is located in `~/projects/foo/.eslintrc` and uses plugin `blah`
3. Subdirectory `~/projects/foo/bar` is the one that has `package.json` and `node_modules` folder, with plugin `eslint-plugin-blah` installed in it.
4. ESLint is run from `~/projects/foo/bar`

This would've worked with old behavior, but it would not find plugin with the new behavior.

And, again, for the record. This also means that even if you have ESLint installed globally, you should install plugins and configs locally, relative to the location of the `.eslintrc` file. This is a major breaking change from previous behavior (not necessarily a bad one, just major change).
Yes, just wanted all of the changes noted in one place.

I vote for solution 3: using `require`.

I read again the following docs:
- [Configuration Cascading and Hierarchy](http://eslint.org/docs/user-guide/configuring#configuration-cascading-and-hierarchy)
- [Shareable Configs](http://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/shareable-configs)

I recap the complete configuration hierarchy:

1) Inline configuration
2) Command line options
3) Project-level configuration
3.4) In the absence of any configuration from (3.1) thru (3.3), fall back to a personal default configuration in `~/.eslintrc`.
4) NEW - If the config file path and CWD are not in the same hierarchy, just use the default behavior of require.
5) NEW - Global-level configuration (local config extending global plugins/configs), like point 4 (use case #5160).

`require` should resolve both issues, #5160 and #5164 and it should not be a breaking change.

issue.title: New config file plugin/extends resolution not working with node.js API and `configFile` option

labels.name: core
labels.description: Relates to ESLint's core APIs and features

labels.name: accepted
labels.description: There is consensus among the team that this change meets the criteria for inclusion

labels.name: archived due to age
labels.description: This issue has been archived; please open a new issue for any further discussion

repository.name: eslint
repository.description: Find and fix problems in your JavaScript code.

issue.body:
The file resolution for the `plugin` and `extends` options works differently in eslint 2.0.0.

`standard` 6.0.0 is using `eslint` 2.0.0-rc.0 and the `configFile` option to the node.js API. [The code](https://github.com/feross/standard/blob/39a54d33f95ca564d976ea2cb97f4c3a45ed0c09/options.js) looks roughly like this:

``` js
var CLIEngine = require("eslint").CLIEngine
var cli = new CLIEngine({ configFile: path.join(__dirname, 'rc', '.eslintrc') })
```

This `.eslintrc` file contains:

``` json
{
  "extends": ["standard", "standard-jsx"]
}
```

The `eslint-config-standard` and `eslint-config-standard-jsx` packages are dependencies of the `standard` package, of course. 

The problem is that when users install `standard` as a dependency of their own project and run it, they get the following error:

```
Error: Cannot find module 'eslint-config-standard-jsx' from '/home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2'
Referenced from: /home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2/node_modules/standard/rc/.eslintrc
    at Function.module.exports [as sync] (/home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2/node_modules/standard/node_modules/eslint/node_modules/resolve/lib/sync.js:33:11)
    at resolve (/home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2/node_modules/standard/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:393:38)
    at load (/home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2/node_modules/standard/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:412:24)
    at /home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2/node_modules/standard/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:331:36
    at Array.reduceRight (native)
    at applyExtends (/home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2/node_modules/standard/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:314:28)
    at Object.load (/home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2/node_modules/standard/node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-file.js:436:22)
    at loadConfig (/home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2/node_modules/standard/node_modules/eslint/lib/config.js:67:33)
    at new Config (/home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2/node_modules/standard/node_modules/eslint/lib/config.js:192:38)
    at CLIEngine.executeOnFiles (/home/travis/build/matjaz/stdin2/node_modules/standard/node_modules/eslint/lib/cli-engine.js:492:28)
```

It seems that the `process.cwd()` is being used as starting point for the search, instead of the config file's folder.

Perhaps the `relativeTo` argument is not being passed to the `resolve` function [in this code](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/11435afd76278a1291566c92af985bf8fad0731f/lib/config/config-file.js#L389-L394)?

In any case, this affected `standard` [recently](https://github.com/feross/standard/issues/406) and required [this hack](https://github.com/feross/standard/compare/v6.0.1...v6.0.3) to workaround. Hoping we can figure out a real fix to this.

issue.title: webpack 2 resolves config files relative to the CWD

repository.name: canonical
repository.description: Canonical code style linter and formatter for JavaScript, SCSS, CSS and JSON.

issue.body:
> This is breaking tools such as [Canonical](https://github.com/gajus/canonical) and [Standard](https://github.com/feross/standard).
> 
> A program has its own [`eslintrc.json`](https://github.com/gajus/canonical/blob/v3.0.3/src/syntaxes/js/eslintrc.json). That it then uses to [lint text using CLIEngine](https://github.com/gajus/canonical/blob/v3.0.3/src/syntaxes/js/lintText.js#L7-L18). When > attempting to run the program against an arbitrary code base, I get:
> 
> > Cannot find module 'eslint-config-canonical-lodash' from '/Users/gajus/Documents/dev/gajus/react-outside-event'
> 
> What I expect is for CLIEngine to resolve this plugin against Canonical module, since it is Canonical that is running the `CLIEngine`. However, it appears that `CLIEngine` is picking up the current working directory and therefore cannot resolve the configs.> 

https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/5160#issuecomment-181348151

Track resolution of https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/5164 issue.

body:
Okay, so after digging around in the code a bit, it seems like the best solution is this:

If the config file path is a descendant of the _project path_, then resolve relative to the config file. Otherwise, resolve relative to `__dirname` (which is basically what `require()` does).

The project path is the project that has ESLint installed. For instance:

```
~/projects/my-project
```

That is different than the CWD, because the CWD can change from run to run but the project path won't. I can calculate the project path by looking up the directory structure from `__dirname`.

I believe this will also solve #5160, but need to try it out.

**Tell us about your environment**

* **ESLint Version:**
v4.16.0
* **Node Version:**
v9.4.0
* **npm Version:**
v5.6.0

**What did you do? Please include the actual source code causing the issue, as well as the command that you used to run ESLint.**

This is a follow-up of #9746.
See this repository, which explains the issue: chrisblossom/eslint-issue-9746

**What did you expect to happen?**

ESLint should be able to work inside Lerna projects.

**What actually happened? Please include the actual, raw output from ESLint.**

ESLint throws errors regarding module resolutions.

As described here (https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/9746#issuecomment-356810436) it seems that this is the expected behaviour, however I'd argue that the changes presented here: #9896 are actually improving the module resolution logic, while fixing #9746.

First, it splits up the `extraLookup` path into multiple paths where modules should be looked for, according to Node module specifications.

Secondly, the change to `getBaseDir` seems pretty straightforward: the `projectPath` should not be a `node_modules` directory.

If those changes are accepted, it would actually resolve issues users have with ESLint and Lerna, while improving the module resolution logic.
